title: Inspect remotes
summary: A remote is a named address for another repository. Viewing remotes does not upload or download commits.
introduction: A remote is a named address for another repository. Viewing remotes does not upload or download commits. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A remote is a named address for another repository. Viewing remotes does not upload or download commits.
A new local repository may show no remotes. This is normal and does not stop local commits.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Explain what the common name origin refers to.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Do not paste secret tokens into remote URLs.
For more detail later, use this [Git further reading](https://git-scm.com/docs/gittutorial).
